anchor.text: // Our profile corrections are the file's own (DNG-embedded) ones, which Lightroom applies

findings.failureScenario: crs.rs:396-398, files.rs:47-49 ('These are the only "profile" corrections Ember applies'), docs/xmp-interop.md:138 and docs/gaps.md:29 ('No lens profile database') all say profile corrections are only the file's own embedded ones. Since lens_profiles::for_raw (lens_profiles.rs:63-71) a lensfun-format database (LIGHTCRAFT_LENSFUN_DIR) also fills Photo.embedded_lens, which turns optics.lens_profile on by default (catalog model.rs:418-420). The XMP mapper's rule, built on the stale premise, ignores LensProfileEnable=0, so with a database configured a Lightroom sidecar/LRCAT edit that had profile corrections off imports with database distortion/vignetting correction on: the geometry and the imported crop no longer match the source edit.
findings.action: Update the comments in crs.rs and files.rs, docs/xmp-interop.md:138 and docs/gaps.md row 8 to cover database profiles; in crs::to_partial carry LensProfileEnable=0 over when the photo's correction came from the database rather than the file (or record the source of embedded_lens so the mapper can tell).

anchor.text: /// Import into the current library. Existing edited records are preserved unless explicitly

findings.failureScenario: The import contract says 'Existing edited records are preserved unless explicitly requested' (lightroom_catalog.rs:743) and 'Existing edited photos are preserved unless updateExisting=true' (library.importLightroom, cmd/library.rs:1391). In apply_prepared only develop settings are kept (keep_develop, 864-914); for every photo already in the library it unconditionally emits SetRating, SetFlag, SetLabel, SetMeta (keywords replaced wholesale at 891, XMP metadata merged at 875) and SetCaptured (915-922). Re-importing a catalog with updateExisting=false therefore silently overwrites ratings, picks, labels, keywords, metadata and capture-time corrections the user made in Ember, contrary to the documented default (recoverable only by undoing the whole import step).
findings.action: Either gate the rating/flag/label/meta/captured ops on update_existing (or on the photo being unedited) to match the contract, or narrow the doc comment, command help and docs/lightroom-catalog-import.md to say only develop edits are preserved.
findings.sourceQuote: Existing edited photos are preserved unless updateExisting=true

anchor.text: //! published primaries and curves, optional output sharpening and a JPEG file-size limit. Pure (bytes in, bytes out) so the desktop

findings.failureScenario: The module doc claims export is 'Pure (bytes in, bytes out) ... writing the file is the caller's job', but the module reads originals from disk (PreparedExport::run, export.rs:1817), owns the native file writer (write_file/write_file_durable, 1991-2008, creating folders and replacing files), and reserves/drives Apple Photos imports (after_export, 1954-1970). A caller relying on the documented purity (e.g. reusing it in the web build or a sandboxed context) gets filesystem and osascript side effects it was told it would not.
findings.action: Rewrite the module doc to state the actual boundary (pure encoders plus session-bound export orchestration, file I/O and post-processing), or move write_file/AfterExport/PreparedExport file reads into a separate module so the pure claim holds for what remains.
